headline: I Am The Intern Tasked With Photoshop-Converting Entire Global Geographies Into American Suburbs
body:
My internship began with high hopes of managing social media calendars, but last Tuesday, I was handed a laptop, a cracked copy of a creative suite, and a mandate to turn the Strait of Hormuz into a manicured gated community complete with white picket fences and a Taco Bell. My supervisor didn't ask for geographical accuracy; he just wanted to know if I could ‘soften the edges’ of the coastline and maybe add a few golden retrievers frolicking on the tankers.

I’ve spent the last 48 hours layering high-resolution suburban lawns over international shipping lanes. The hardest part wasn't the technical work—it was figuring out how to replace the dark, turbulent waters with a shimmering, chlorinated community pool reflection. When I suggested that a sprawling naval chokepoint might be structurally incompatible with a cul-de-sac, I was told that the 'vision' requires total commitment to the aesthetic of a neighborhood Homeowners Association.

By Thursday morning, I was deep into the 'territory annexation' phase, which mostly involves photoshopping manicured hedges over international maritime borders. My thumb is cramped from masking out massive oil tankers and replacing them with golf carts and luxury SUVs. If the world looks like a serene, suburban wasteland tomorrow, just know that I’m doing my best to fix the lighting on the lampposts, even if the geopolitical implications are completely beyond my pay grade.
caption: When the internship description says 'creative digital asset management,' it really just means painting over global hotspots with suburban tranquility. #InternLife #GraphicDesign #Geopolitics #StraitOfHormuz (satire)
igHook: Would you move to a gated community in the middle of a major global shipping lane?
imagePrompt: A close-up of a computer monitor showing a professional photo editing interface, with an image of a rugged coastal strait partially covered by digital layers of suburban housing developments and grassy lawns.

sourceHeadline.title: Trump Posts AI Photo Of Hormuz As "New US Territory", Says All Mines Removed

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 10 succeeds by shifting the perspective from the 'scammed buyer' trope—which appears repeatedly in this batch—to the cynical, absurd reality of the 'intern' tasked with making global war zones look like American suburbs. It avoids the repetitive AI-purchased-property formula, introduces specific and vivid creative detail, and maintains a distinct voice that feels fresher than the rest of the cohort.
